data.hook: Imagine an AI that spots a scientific question, gathers evidence, tests ideas, and updates its beliefs—all on its own. Perplexity AI just committed massive resources to make that real.
data.name: Perplexity Launches Frontier Research with 10,000 GPUs for Autonomous AI Scientists
data.summary: Perplexity AI unveiled Frontier Research today, dedicating over 10,000 GPUs to build automated systems that handle the complete cycle of scientific inquiry, from hypothesis formation to experimentation. CEO Aravind Srinivas and Research Lead Andrew Gordon Wilson emphasized open-sourcing models, publishing papers, and inviting collaboration on multi-agent systems and continual learning. The team is hiring in San Francisco, Palo Alto, New York, and London, with applications due by December 5, aiming to accelerate research through real-world testing in Perplexity products.

data.name: Stanford Professors Launch Noeri with $110M for Custom Self-Improving AI
data.summary: Noeri emerged from stealth on November 16, 2026, with a massive $110 million seed round led by Menlo Ventures to build 'plural intelligence'—specialized, self-improving AI systems companies can own and tailor. Their 'AI engineer' reviews client workflows and suggests smart tweaks like better tools or smaller models, all with clear explanations for approval, helping bridge the gap to real business needs. Founders emphasize empowerment, letting teams craft their own AI rather than renting from a few big labs, a vision backed by investors like NVIDIA and early wins in research efficiency.

data.name: Sam Altman Eyes Robot-Built Data Centers to Slash AI Costs
data.summary: On John Collison’s Cheeky Pint podcast, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman shared plans to use robotics for self-replicating data centers, including AI-controlled factories for chips, turbines, and solar panels to produce cheap compute. He highlighted how robots could bypass permitting delays and supply chain issues, building on OpenAI's in-house chip and data center work. The idea drew mixed reactions, with some lamenting fewer construction jobs than promised, amid broader questions on AI's economic impact and automation's workforce effects.

data.hook: Tech investors woke up to a sharp reality check Monday as forecasts for massive AI spending took a big hit. Nvidia shares plunged over 5% in premarket, wiping out nearly $2 trillion in value since their October peak.
data.name: SemiAnalysis Cuts AI Chip Spending Forecasts, Tech Stocks Slide
data.summary: Semiconductor research firm SemiAnalysis sharply lowered its long-term AI accelerator spending projections, with 2028 estimates dropping 28% to $758 billion and 2030 falling 40% to $923 billion. The revisions, driven by slower revenue growth at AI labs, tighter capital markets, and U.S. election delays, hit Nvidia hardest, accounting for 66% of reduced shipments through 2030. Even after cuts, spending is still set to more than double by 2030, though markets reacted with Nasdaq 100 futures down 1.7% ahead of Nvidia's earnings.

data.name: Silicon Valley Races to Build AI Agent Swarms
data.summary: Silicon Valley developers and investors are pushing agent swarms—coordinated groups of AI agents that handle search, payments, memory, and more through new tools and market maps from a16z. Tools like Swarms Corp's AgentRearrange and Google's Antigravity let builders create multi-agent workflows with simple code, spawning coordinators, workers, and verifiers that debate and test in real time. While token costs and coordination challenges persist, the rapid rise of these systems has experts rethinking how companies organize, favoring swarm-native setups over traditional ones.

data.name: OpenAI Explored $5 Billion Goodfire Acquisition This Summer
data.summary: Goodfire, a 2023-founded specialist in mechanistic interpretability, caught OpenAI's eye for its tools that peer inside neural networks to spot hidden dangers like cyberattacks. Talks this summer aimed at a $5 billion valuation—four times its recent $1.25 billion funding round—but fell through as Goodfire chose independence to serve multiple AI labs. Backed by investors like Anthropic and Menlo Ventures, the startup already partners with Microsoft and others, highlighting the push for safer AI through transparent 'black box' analysis.

data.hook: Companies once stuck with one AI provider are now mixing models like pros, with open-weight options surging in use.
data.name: Enterprises Rapidly Shift to Multi-Model AI Strategies
data.summary: Databricks' new AI Index, based on traffic from over 10,000 enterprises, shows open-weight models jumping from 7.3% to 30.9% of token traffic in just 3.5 months. Today, 75% of firms use two or more providers, and half use three or more, favoring models like DeepSeek and Zhipu for coding and batch tasks. Leaders like Patrick Wendell and CEO Ali Ghodsi call the changes striking, as task-specific routing—such as Claude for planning and OpenAI for editing—becomes standard, pointing to a market optimizing for cost and fit over single-lab loyalty.

Leaders from TensorWave, AMD, and OpenAI emphasized how it meets surging demand for reliable, massive-scale AI compute to advance frontier models worldwide.

Developers integrate via SDKs, shifting focus from building tools to hiring the right agent.

data.hook: Imagine your AI helper hunting down the perfect gift, filling the cart, and ready to buy—with you giving the final nod via fingerprint. OpenAI just made that real for some users.
data.name: OpenAI Launches ChatGPT Wallet for AI-Agent Purchases
data.summary: ChatGPT Wallet lets AI agents called 'dots' handle online shopping for Pro subscribers in the US, starting November 13. Users link a credit card once securely, and the agent searches, adds items, and preps checkout, but every purchase requires biometric approval like Face ID to show details and confirm. Built with AmEx, Mastercard, and Visa, it uses one-time tokens for safety, keeps card rewards intact, and works only in dot conversations for those 18+ with eligible US cards. Early users praise the human oversight for simple buys like reorders, while skeptics flag privacy worries and potential checkout glitches as retailers adapt.

data.name: Telus Drops Two Vancouver AI Data Centre Projects Amid Local Pushback
data.summary: Telus confirmed it will no longer co-develop two Vancouver sites—a 10-storey facility near BC Place and a conversion in Mount Pleasant—with real estate firm Westbank. The projects were part of a May-announced sovereign AI cluster using tens of thousands of Nvidia chips and up to 163 megawatts of power, including heat recovery for nearby homes. A source linked the withdrawal to local opposition and shifts in Telus's AI strategy, while Westbank plans to proceed with a new partner. Reactions ranged from NDP leader Avi Lewis celebrating a community victory to critics like Jason Kenney warning of risks to Canadian data sovereignty.

data.hook: Teams at Linear now let AI agents handle over half of code reviews alongside just the author, freeing humans for bigger challenges.
data.name: AI Reviews Hit 53% of Code Merges at Linear
data.summary: By October 2026, 53% of Linear's code changes merged with only an author and AI reviewer, up from near zero earlier in the year. Industry-wide, human-reviewed pull requests dropped from 98% to 47% between May and October. While some worry about 'comprehension debt' from rapid AI-generated features, Linear engineers found fewer bugs and reverts with strong testing. Satya Nadella noted verification and specification as the new key skills in building software factories with AI.
